about: The priest's own prayer, said secretly, bowed over the middle of the altar with his hands joined upon it. The Mass has already been dismissed; what is left he says for himself. The whole prayer stands in the first person singular — servitútis meæ, óbtuli, mihíque — and asks two things: that the service rendered may please God, and that the sacrifice may win favour for himself and for those he offered it for. With the offertory's “Súscipe, sancta Trínitas” it is one of the two prayers of the Mass that address the Trinity by name. In Masses for the Dead no blessing is given, and the Pláceat is said all the same.

s01.narrative: Then the celebrant bows before the middle of the altar, joins his hands upon it, and says secretly:

s02.translation: May the homage of my service please Thee, O holy Trinity; and grant that the sacrifice which I, unworthy, have offered before the eyes of Thy majesty may be acceptable to Thee, and may win favour, through Thy mercy, for me and for all those for whom I have offered it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: The subject is not the priest but “obséquium” (w005), the homage — that is what is to please God.

w004.function: Vocative. Apart from the offertory this is the only place in the Mass where a prayer addresses the Trinity by name.

w007.function: Agrees with “servitútis” (w006). First person singular: here the priest speaks for himself, not for the assembly.

w012.function: Neuter, agreeing with “sacrifícium” (w011), and object of “óbtuli” (w017).

w013.function: The form is dative and ablative at once, and the sentence does not choose: with “óbtuli” (w017) the dative would give offered TO the eyes of Thy majesty, the ablative offered BEFORE them. The corpus claims no case here.

w016.function: Nominative: it describes the man who offers, not the offering — “I, unworthy, have offered”.

w020.function: Neuter, because what it says is said of “sacrifícium” (w011).

w021.function: One written word carrying two: mihi with the conjunction -que hung on the end, “and for me”. That -que pulls the stress onto the syllable just before it.

w029.function: With “miseránte” (w030) it forms an ablative absolute, which English turns into a clause: “Thou showing mercy”, that is, through Thy mercy.

w030.function: A deponent participle: active in form, as the present participles of deponents always are.

w031.function: A rare and late word; of the two Latin lexicons the corpus consults, only one carries it.
